about: A reshuffled Zork I. I entered the white house through the window and went down the trap door to the cellar and the troll. The lantern and sword start in different places, the troll gets bribed with food, and a cave leads down into underground caverns.

done.why: I died to the troll, was reborn in the forest, and robbed the egg. I played about 20 turns and stopped there.

moments.note: The trap door slammed shut behind me and I heard it being barred.
The troll gladly ate the pepper sack I gave it, though it kept attacking.
I attacked the troll and died within one turn. I woke in the forest with the sword on the ground and my other items gone.
Opening the egg with the sword gave a vivid, funny description of the ruined canary.
The troll ate the sack but still blocked the way. I could not tell what the gift had changed.

wished: Give the troll the bottle of water without having to open it first.
Find out what the sack did to the troll.
Get my items back after dying.

lines.line: The trap door crashes shut, and you hear someone barring it.
lines.why: A familiar moment, made more ominous by the barring.

lines.line: The troll, who is not overly proud, graciously accepts the gift and not having the most discriminating tastes, gleefully eats it.
lines.why: Funny, and it showed the troll reacts to what you give it.

lines.line: Conquering his fears, the troll puts you to death.

fun.why: The oddball commands worked and got witty replies. My short run ended in an abrupt death and a quick exit.

engagement.why: The troll was a good hook, but I only explored a little.

difficulty.why: The troll killed me in one blow, which was harsh, but I was reckless.

interestingness.why: The changes were small: the lantern and sword were moved, and the troll acted differently. I did not see much of the rest.

prose.why: The prose is crisp and witty, and the egg description stood out.
